title: A deep dive into exe.dev
partialText: exe.dev gives you persistent Linux VMs over SSH, each with an HTTPS URL, private-by-default sharing, and a built-in coding agent. How it works, what it costs, and how I use it.

title: Zustand: simple React state management
partialText: Learn Zustand through a React store: actions, selectors, immutable updates, persistence, testing, SSR boundaries, and when local or server state is better.

title: Content Security Policy (CSP) explained
partialText: Build and deploy a Content Security Policy with source directives, nonces or hashes, report-only rollout, framing protection, testing, and common CSP mistakes.

title: Passkeys and WebAuthn explained
partialText: Understand passkeys and WebAuthn, then build registration and login with server challenges, stored public keys, SimpleWebAuthn, recovery, and tests.

title: Introduction to TanStack Query
partialText: Learn TanStack Query from the server-state mental model through query keys, freshness, errors, mutations, invalidation, optimistic updates, and common mistakes.

title: Build a documentation site with Astro and Markdown
partialText: Build a fast documentation site with Astro, Markdown collections, generated navigation, previous and next links, search, and a sitemap.

title: How to let an AI agent perform irreversible actions safely
partialText: A practical architecture for AI agents that spend money, deploy code, delete data, or change infrastructure without turning confirmation into a suggestion.

title: Build a chatbot with Cloudflare Workers AI
partialText: Build and deploy a Workers AI chatbot with the AI binding, validated conversation history, streaming responses, rate limits, cost controls, and state choices.

title: What happens when Bun runs a TypeScript file
partialText: Follow bun run app.ts through CLI dispatch, module resolution, TypeScript transpilation, JavaScriptCore, Node compatibility, and the event loop.

title: A deep dive into Cloudflare Images
partialText: How Cloudflare Images works: resize, convert and crop images with a URL or a Worker, store uploads, serve private images, and what it costs. Lots of examples.

title: How to stream LLM responses with server-sent events
partialText: Stream LLM text from a provider through your server to the browser with SSE, a correct buffered parser, cancellation, errors, security, and production checks.

title: Run a local LLM with Ollama
partialText: Run an LLM locally with Ollama, choose a model that fits, call the chat API from Node.js, stream replies, request JSON, and understand the limits.

title: Use AI to understand code
partialText: The best use of AI is not generating more code. Ask focused questions, attack a change from every angle, and keep the mental model. Code is the byproduct.

title: How to build an LLM from scratch
partialText: A practical guide for software engineers to build and train a small GPT-style language model on a Mac with Language Model Builder.

title: Biome: one tool for linting and formatting
partialText: Biome replaces ESLint and Prettier with one fast Rust tool. Install with biome init, run biome check, and migrate your existing config.

title: Email for developers and AI agents: how to choose a provider
partialText: Compare Resend, Cloudflare Email Service, Postmark, Mailgun, SendGrid, Amazon SES, Mailtrap and AgentMail for sending, receiving, and giving AI agents an inbox.

title: What is an AGENTS.md file
partialText: Use AGENTS.md to give coding agents durable project instructions, from commands and conventions to scoped rules, verification, maintenance, and common mistakes.

title: How to build an MCP server
partialText: Build and test a TypeScript MCP server with one useful tool, stdio transport, input validation, clear errors, timeouts, and client configuration.

title: SSH for developers
partialText: SSH for developers: connect to VPS servers, create keys with ssh-keygen, use ~/.ssh/config aliases, and copy files with scp or rsync.

title: How to scan your code with the Codex Security CLI
partialText: Use OpenAI's Codex Security CLI to scan repositories, track vulnerabilities, verify fixes, review changes, and add security checks to CI.

title: Enrollment for the September bootcamp is open
partialText: Enrollment is open for the 10-week September bootcamp. Build and ship real software with AI coding agents, starting from zero.

title: Run Cursor cloud agents on your own Mac mini
partialText: Run Cursor cloud agents on your own Mac mini: install the Cursor CLI, start a self-hosted worker, and send it tasks that run on your hardware.

title: A deep dive into WebMCP
partialText: Learn how WebMCP lets browser agents discover and call tools inside a live web page, using JavaScript, HTML forms, secure boundaries, and tests.

title: The jq command
partialText: Learn the jq command to filter and transform JSON from curl on the CLI. Covers fields, select, map, and raw output with a real API example.

title: A deep dive into ZCode
partialText: I tried ZCode with GLM-5.3 on a real project. Here's how the coding agent works, what it costs, its permission modes, automations, API, and limits.

title: A deep dive into Executor
partialText: Learn how Executor lets AI agents safely use multiple accounts for the same MCP, OpenAPI, or GraphQL integration through one catalog.

title: Git hooks for AI engineering
partialText: Use Git hooks as deterministic guardrails for AI coding agents, with fast checks before commits, stronger checks before pushes, and CI as the final gate.

title: A deep dive into DeepSec
partialText: Learn how DeepSec scans a repository with AI agents, then follow a real 729-file review that produced 504 findings and a short action list.

title: I built 37 terminal text effects in pure JavaScript
partialText: I built tte.js, a dependency-free browser library that animates text and ASCII art with 37 Canvas effects.

title: node:sqlite: SQLite built into Node.js
partialText: Use node:sqlite in Node.js to open a database, run prepared statements, query rows, and use in-memory databases for tests without npm packages.
